Reflecting pools lie still between the garden terraces, their surfaces scattered with floating blossoms that glow faintly beneath the water.
Graceful fountains shaped as leaping deer and outstretched herons pour silver water into moss-rimmed basins from carved mouths.
Graceful statues of ancient elf-lords stand at every gate, their carved faces serene, faint motes of fae light drifting at their feet.
Flowering creepers of white and pale violet drape every archway and balustrade, filling the air with a soft persistent sweetness.
Thin spires rise at every corner, each tipped with a soft radiant glow like a candle held cupped inside pale glass.
Glowing crystal lamps hang at intervals along the colonnades, their faceted surfaces scattering slow spinning fragments of prismatic light.
Woven-branch archways frame the garden entrances, draped in drifting golden motes that settle and rise like embers without heat or ash.
Carved stone cornices run the length of every roofline, shaped into an unbroken procession of oak leaves, acorns, and twisting stems.
Bridges of pale birchwood lashed with living cord cross the garden canals, their planks soft with silver moss underfoot.
Enormous ancient oaks grow up through the open floors of the great halls, their canopies spreading across the vaulted ceilings above.
Fae-light pools in shallow stone cups carved into the parapets, steady and soft as breathing, untouched by any wind or rain.
Long colonnades of slender pale pillars line the main avenues, each column wound with a climbing rose frozen into white stone.
Doorways are framed by living hedges trimmed to arch overhead, tiny luminous flowers woven through the dark foliage like scattered sparks.
Thin chains of hammered silver link spire to spire overhead, hung with small bells that ring with a clear and sourceless tone.
The great hall floors are inlaid with pale moonstone and dark jade in patterns of spreading ferns and interlocked branches.
Shallow stepped terraces descend from the citadel to the river, each tier edged with flowering white stone and soft glowing pools.
Motes of silver fae-light drift slowly upward through the open courts at dusk, rising past the spires and dissolving into the darkening sky.
Delicate spiral staircases wind upward through hollow spire-cores, their steps carved with tiny flowering vines that seem to bloom in moonlight.
Gossamer banners of pale silk drift between the towers, embroidered with silver thread that catches and holds fae light long after dusk.
Glowing vines of deep emerald climb the outer tower walls, pulsing gently with warm inner light as though breathing in the dark.
Warm amber light spills through tall narrow windows of thin-cut crystal, casting honeyed patterns across the pale stone courtyards below.
Reflecting pools of perfectly still water mirror the spires above, their surfaces scattered with softly glowing lily-pads of fae origin.
Graceful stone statues of elf-lords line the grand processional avenues, carved in such fine detail their robes seem to stir in the breeze.
Flowering creepers of pale white and violet cascade down every outer wall, filling the city air with a sweet persistent fragrance.
Thin tapered spires rise at every roofline, each tipped with a soft orb of gathered fae-light that never dims through the night.
Glowing crystal lamps rest within carved stone alcoves along every corridor, their blue-white light steady and cool as captured winter moonshine.
Woven-branch archways of living willow frame the city gates, hung thick with drifting golden motes that cling like slow-falling embers.
